title: Updates on Tariffs, Liquidity, and Strategy
summary: Tariff pressure and Strategy’s preferred-share financing.
assessment: The TGA undershoot forecast was wrong. The preferred-share analysis correctly distinguishes maturity risk from dividend deferral, but overstates par stability and eventual recovery. STRC grew substantially while its yield rose rather than converging toward seven percent; STRF and STRC delivered very different returns.

claims.claim: Tariffs impose material domestic costs.
claims.reason: The static goods-import arithmetic is internally consistent and subsequent research found nearly 90% of tariff incidence fell on US firms and consumers. This does not imply that unchanged import-price indexes prove zero foreign burden in every sector or that static revenue would be collected.

evidence.title: Tariff incidence and pass-through
evidence.finding: Domestic firms and consumers bore nearly 90% of the burden.

claims.claim: Factory spending measures replacement needs.
claims.reason: Flat industrial output does not establish that a historical construction spending level equals replacement cost. Output can be flat while capacity, utilization, capital intensity, prices and equipment investment change. Building construction excludes major components of the productive capital stock.

claims.reason: Issuing shares above net asset value and buying the same underlying asset can increase assets per share after costs. claims.claim: Preferreds reduce maturity-driven failure risk.
claims.reason: Perpetual preferreds remove a scheduled principal maturity and dividends can generally be deferred without a bond default. This reduces one failure channel while raising recurring distribution needs and leaving asset, market-price and funding risks. It does not eliminate all redemption or change-of-control provisions.
